name: Ornamental plate armour
description: A full suit of decorative plate made for a hallway or a stage, not a fight: thin cheap iron etched with brass-coloured bands, a boss on the chest and rust eating through. The leather straps are rotten and it weighs a ton, but it still turns a blade.
notes: Laid out front up, neck towards -z, 780 mm across and 890 mm from the pauldrons to the ankles: the leg harnesses (curved thigh plate, domed knee cop, calf-shaped greave) under the breastplate, which sits on a flat backplate with a ridge down the middle and lames at the waist; an arm harness of two tubes and an elbow cop either side, a domed pauldron with two lames at each shoulder, and buckled leather straps on every piece. Iron in `iron-dull` with `rust-red` patches, brass-coloured etched bands round the neck and waist and down the chest, a raised boss, three waist lames and long frayed strap ends. CHECK LENGTH: the reference gives 600 mm; laid out the suit is 890 mm. Slot `vest` follows the cardboard armour and earlier armour batches, though the suit also covers the arms and legs; Deadvox has no whole-body armour slot. Protection is a judgement for thin, brittle iron: worse than real plate, and the high encumbrance follows the reference. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.
